questions.stem: Typical dexmedetomidine maintenance infusion?
questions.explanation: Dexmedetomidine, infusion: 0.2–0.7 mcg/kg/hr. 25–75 mcg/kg/min is the propofol sedation rate. 0.05–0.1 mcg/kg/hr is too low to sedate. 1.5–2 mcg/kg/hr is above the usual maximum. ICU sedation may go up to 1.5 mcg/kg/hr.

questions.stem: Maximum daily ketorolac dose for adults under 65?
questions.explanation: Ketorolac, adult daily max: 120 mg. 30 mg is a single dose. 60 mg is the maximum for age 65 or older. 240 mg is double the maximum.

questions.stem: Concentration of 50% magnesium sulfate?
questions.explanation: Magnesium sulfate 50%: 500 mg/mL. 100 mg/mL is 10% calcium salts. 40 mg/mL is a 40 g/1,000 mL preeclampsia bag. 200 mg/mL is 20% mannitol. Source: Standard percent conversion.

questions.stem: Regular insulin dose for hyperkalemia in ESRD?
questions.explanation: Insulin, hyperkalemia in ESRD: 5 units. 10 units is the standard dose. 15 units is excessive. 2 units is too low.

questions.stem: Typical adult IV succinylcholine intubating dose?
questions.explanation: Succinylcholine, adult IV: 1–1.5 mg/kg. 2 mg/kg is the infant dose. 0.6 mg/kg is the rocuronium intubating dose. 3–4 mg/kg is the IM dose range.

questions.stem: Oral aprepitant dose for PONV prophylaxis?
questions.explanation: Aprepitant, PONV: 40 mg. 125 mg is the chemotherapy day-1 dose. 4 mg is the ondansetron dose. 80 mg is the chemotherapy day 2–3 dose.

questions.stem: First pediatric adenosine dose?
questions.explanation: Adenosine, pediatric: 0.1 mg/kg. 0.02 mg/kg is the pediatric atropine dose. 0.2 mg/kg is the second pediatric dose. 0.05 mg/kg is half the first dose.

questions.stem: Neostigmine reversal dose range (FDA label)?
questions.explanation: Neostigmine, reversal: 0.03–0.07 mg/kg. 0.01–0.02 mg/kg is closer to the glycopyrrolate pairing dose. 0.5–1 mg/kg is the edrophonium dose. 0.1–0.15 mg/kg is above the labeled maximum. Source: Bloxiverz FDA label; 0.03 for shallow block or shorter-acting relaxants, 0.07 for deeper block or longer-acting relaxants.

questions.stem: Maximum dose of plain lidocaine?
questions.explanation: Lidocaine plain, max: 4.5 mg/kg. 2.5 mg/kg is the plain bupivacaine maximum. 7 mg/kg is the maximum with epinephrine. 3 mg/kg is the ropivacaine maximum.

questions.stem: Concentration of methylergonovine?
questions.explanation: Methylergonovine vial: 0.2 mg/mL. 0.25 mg/mL is carboprost's concentration in mg. 1 mg/mL is terbutaline's concentration. 0.4 mg/mL is atropine's concentration. Source: Methylergonovine labeling.

questions.stem: Concentration of D50?
questions.explanation: Dextrose 50%: 0.5 g/mL. 0.05 g/mL is D5W. 5 g/mL is a misplaced decimal. 0.1 g/mL is D10W. Source: Standard percent conversion.

questions.stem: Midazolam induction dose range (label, premedicated adults)?
questions.explanation: Midazolam, induction: 0.15–0.35 mg/kg. 0.02–0.04 mg/kg is the premedication range. 1–2 mg/kg is the ketamine IV induction dose. 0.05–0.1 mg/kg is a sedation-range dose. Source: midazolam labeling; unpremedicated adults under 55 need 0.3–0.35 mg/kg.

questions.stem: Amiodarone first dose in pulseless VF?
questions.explanation: Amiodarone, pulseless: 300 mg. 75 mg is too low. 150 mg is the stable VT and second arrest dose. 450 mg is above the arrest dose.

questions.stem: Low-dose naloxone infusion rate for neuraxial opioid pruritus?
questions.explanation: Naloxone, pruritus infusion: 0.25–1 mcg/kg/hr. 1–2 mcg/kg is a bolus for respiratory depression. 3–5 mcg/kg/hr is enough to reverse analgesia. 2.5–5 mg is the nalbuphine pruritus dose.

questions.stem: Typical nitroglycerin infusion rate?
questions.explanation: Nitroglycerin, infusion: 10–200 mcg/min. 1–5 mcg/min is too low. 500–1,000 mcg/min is excessive. 0.3–10 mcg/kg/min is the nitroprusside range.

questions.stem: Pediatric IV epinephrine dose in cardiac arrest?
questions.explanation: Epinephrine, pediatric arrest: 0.01 mg/kg. 0.1 mg/kg is the endotracheal dose, not IV. 0.02 mg/kg is the pediatric atropine dose. 0.05 mg/kg is above the IV dose.

questions.stem: Onset of IV adenosine given as a rapid push?
questions.explanation: Adenosine, onset: Seconds. 30–60 sec is epinephrine's onset. 1–2 min is too slow for adenosine. 5 min is far too slow. Source: Adenosine labeling.

questions.stem: Fentanyl loading dose range on the reference sheet (moderate-dose technique)?
questions.explanation: Fentanyl, induction: 2–20 mcg/kg. 0.1–0.5 mcg/kg is the sufentanil range. 0.5–2 mcg/kg/hr is the infusion range. 50–100 mcg/kg is the labeled sole-anesthetic dose. Source: fentanyl labeling (moderate dose) and the USAGPAN sheet.

questions.stem: Typical isoproterenol infusion range?
questions.explanation: Isoproterenol, infusion: 2–10 mcg/min. 50–200 mcg is the phenylephrine bolus. 20–40 mcg/min is excessive. 0.2–0.5 mcg/min is too low.

questions.stem: Pediatric ondansetron dose (max 4 mg)?
questions.explanation: Ondansetron, pediatric: 0.1 mg/kg. 0.15 mg/kg is the pediatric dexamethasone dose. 0.2 mg/kg is double the usual dose. 0.05 mg/kg is half the usual dose.

questions.stem: Concentration of terbutaline?
questions.explanation: Terbutaline vial: 1 mg/mL. 0.25 mg/mL is its dose misread as a concentration. 250 mcg/mL is carboprost's concentration. 0.2 mg/mL is methylergonovine's concentration. Source: Terbutaline labeling.

questions.stem: Typical phenylephrine IV bolus?
questions.explanation: Phenylephrine, bolus: 50–200 mcg. 10–20 mcg is too small to raise BP. 5–10 mg is the ephedrine bolus. 500–1,000 mcg is enough to cause severe hypertension.

questions.stem: Vecuronium maintenance dose (FDA label)?
questions.explanation: Vecuronium, maintenance: 0.01–0.015 mg/kg. 0.1–0.2 mg/kg is the rocuronium redose. 0.04–0.06 mg/kg is the initial dose after a succinylcholine intubation. 0.1 mg/kg is the intubating dose. Source: vecuronium FDA label. The USAGPAN sheet lists 0.05 mg/kg, which is above the labeled maintenance dose.

questions.stem: Concentration of sugammadex?
questions.explanation: Sugammadex vial: 100 mg/mL. 20 mg/mL is succinylcholine's concentration. 50 mg/mL is a ketamine concentration. 10 mg/mL is rocuronium's concentration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: IV vitamin K dose for urgent warfarin reversal?
questions.explanation: Vitamin K, warfarin reversal: 5–10 mg. 0.5 mg is too low. 20–25 mg is excessive. 1–2.5 mg is a low oral dose for mild INR elevation.

questions.stem: Onset of cisatracurium at an intubating dose?
questions.explanation: Cisatracurium, onset: 2–3 min. 30–60 sec is succinylcholine's onset. 60–90 sec is close to rocuronium's onset. 8–10 min is too slow. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: First IV labetalol dose for severe hypertension in pregnancy?
questions.explanation: Labetalol, preeclampsia first dose: 20 mg. 10 mg is a smaller general intraop increment. 80 mg is the third dose. 40 mg is the second dose.

questions.stem: Onset of IV neostigmine?
questions.explanation: Neostigmine, onset: 1–5 min. 60–120 min is neostigmine's duration. 20–30 sec is edrophonium-like speed. 15–20 min is too slow for onset. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Concentration of etomidate?
questions.explanation: Etomidate vial: 2 mg/mL. 10 mg/mL is propofol's concentration. 5 mg/mL is a midazolam concentration. 1 mg/mL is a midazolam concentration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Onset of IV midazolam?
questions.explanation: Midazolam, IV onset: 30–120 sec. 10–15 min is dexmedetomidine's onset. 5–10 sec is too fast for midazolam. 15–80 min is midazolam's duration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Concentration of Ryanodex after reconstitution (250 mg in 5 mL)?
questions.explanation: Ryanodex reconstituted: 50 mg/mL. 250 mg/mL is the vial content misread as a concentration. 5 mg/mL is a 50 mL dilution. 0.33 mg/mL is reconstituted Dantrium (20 mg in 60 mL). Source: Ryanodex labeling.

questions.stem: Typical epinephrine infusion rate?
questions.explanation: Epinephrine, infusion: 0.01–0.1 mcg/kg/min. 2–20 mcg/kg/min is the dobutamine range. 0.5–1 mcg/kg/min is excessive. 0.001–0.005 mcg/kg/min is too low.

questions.stem: Typical IV metoprolol increment?
questions.explanation: Metoprolol, increment: 2.5–5 mg. 25 mg is an oral dose. 0.5–1 mg is too small. 15 mg is the cumulative limit.

questions.stem: Adult daily acetaminophen maximum?
questions.explanation: Acetaminophen, adult daily max: 4 g. 6 g is excessive. 2 g is a reduced limit for heavy alcohol use. 3 g is a conservative limit some protocols use.

questions.stem: Epinephrine concentration in a 1:100,000 solution?
questions.explanation: Epinephrine 1:100,000: 10 mcg/mL. 5 mcg/mL is 1:200,000. 2.5 mcg/mL is 1:400,000. 20 mcg/mL is 1:50,000. Source: Standard ratio conversion.

questions.stem: Methylergonovine IM dose for atony?
questions.explanation: Methylergonovine, IM: 0.2 mg. 0.5 mg is above the usual dose. 0.25 mg is the terbutaline dose. 2 mg is the carboprost cumulative maximum.

questions.stem: Propofol induction dose for an older, debilitated, or ASA 3–4 adult (FDA label)?
questions.explanation: Propofol, older or ASA 3–4 induction: 1–1.5 mg/kg. 2.5–3.5 mg/kg is the pediatric induction dose. 0.25–0.5 mg/kg is sedation-size increments. 2–2.5 mg/kg is the healthy adult dose. Source: Diprivan FDA label.

questions.stem: Initial IV digoxin loading dose?
questions.explanation: Digoxin, initial load: 0.25–0.5 mg. 2 mg is excessive. 0.0625–0.125 mg is the daily maintenance dose. 1–1.5 mg is the full cumulative load given at once.

questions.stem: Peak effect of IV ondansetron?
questions.explanation: Ondansetron, peak: 2 hr. <30 min is ondansetron's onset. 6–12 hr is dexamethasone's peak. 12 hr is ondansetron's duration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Onset of IV glycopyrrolate?
questions.explanation: Glycopyrrolate, onset: 1 min. 10 min is too slow. 5 min is glycopyrrolate's peak. 2–3 hr is glycopyrrolate's duration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Maximum dose of chloroprocaine with epinephrine?
questions.explanation: Chloroprocaine with epi, max: 14 mg/kg. 20 mg/kg is above any cited maximum. 11 mg/kg is the plain maximum. 7 mg/kg is the lidocaine with epinephrine maximum.

questions.stem: Usual subanesthetic ketamine infusion for acute pain (ASRA/AAPM/ASA 2018)?
questions.explanation: Ketamine, analgesic infusion: 0.1–0.5 mg/kg/hr. 0.2–0.7 mcg/kg/hr is the dexmedetomidine infusion. 2–3 mg/kg/hr is above the 1 mg/kg/hr ceiling. 0.01–0.05 mg/kg/hr is too low to help. Source: Schwenk et al. 2018; infusions generally stay at or below 1 mg/kg/hr without intensive monitoring.

questions.stem: Typical small IV oxytocin bolus at cesarean delivery?
questions.explanation: Oxytocin, IV bolus: 1–3 units. 20–40 units is the amount added to a liter for infusion. 0.2 units is too small. 10 units is a large IV push that causes hypotension.

questions.stem: Remifentanil labeled maintenance infusion range?
questions.explanation: Remifentanil, infusion: 0.05–2 mcg/kg/min. 0.5–2 mcg/kg/hr is the fentanyl infusion range. 0.2–0.7 mcg/kg/hr is the dexmedetomidine infusion. 5–10 mcg/kg/min is far above the labeled range. Source: Ultiva FDA label; usual starting rate 0.25 mcg/kg/min.

questions.stem: Typical oral clonidine dose?
questions.explanation: Clonidine, oral: 0.1–0.2 mg. 0.5–1 mg is excessive. 0.025 mg is too small. 1 mcg/kg is the dexmedetomidine load.

questions.stem: Onset of IV atropine?
questions.explanation: Atropine, onset: 1 min. 30–60 min is atropine's duration. 10 min is too slow. 5 min is glycopyrrolate's peak. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: 20% lipid emulsion infusion rate for LAST in a patient under 70 kg?
questions.explanation: Lipid 20%, infusion under 70 kg: 0.25 mL/kg/min. 0.1 mL/kg/min is too slow. 1.5 mL/kg/min is the bolus amount used as a rate. 1 mL/kg/min is too fast.

questions.stem: Duration of spinal ropivacaine?
questions.explanation: Ropivacaine, spinal duration: 2–3.5 hr. 6–8 hr is too long for a single spinal. 60–70 min is spinal lidocaine's duration. 10–20 min is IV lidocaine's duration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Typical intraoperative IV lidocaine infusion rate?
questions.explanation: Lidocaine, IV infusion: 1–2 mg/kg/hr. 0.1–0.5 mg/kg/hr is the ketamine analgesic infusion. 0.25–0.5 mg/kg/hr is too low. 3–4 mg/kg/hr is above the usual range.

questions.stem: IV amisulpride dose for PONV prophylaxis?
questions.explanation: Amisulpride, prophylaxis: 5 mg. 10 mg is the rescue dose. 2.5 mg is half the prophylaxis dose. 4 mg is the ondansetron dose.

questions.stem: Concentration of labetalol?
questions.explanation: Labetalol vial: 5 mg/mL. 10 mg/mL is esmolol's concentration. 1 mg/mL is metoprolol's concentration. 20 mg/mL is hydralazine's concentration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Sodium bicarbonate dose for severe metabolic acidosis?
questions.explanation: Sodium bicarbonate: 1 mEq/kg. 0.1 mEq/kg is too low. 2–3 mEq/kg is excessive. 0.5 mEq/kg is half the dose.

questions.stem: Typical adult glycopyrrolate antisialagogue dose?
questions.explanation: Glycopyrrolate, antisialagogue: 0.1–0.2 mg. 0.02–0.04 mg is too little to dry secretions. 0.4–0.6 mg is a reversal-pairing amount. 1 mg is the atropine bradycardia dose.

questions.stem: Duration of epidural lidocaine?
questions.explanation: Lidocaine, epidural duration: 60–120 min. 2–3 hr is spinal bupivacaine's duration. 10–20 min is IV lidocaine's duration. 120–200 min is epidural bupivacaine's duration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Magnesium maintenance rate for preeclampsia?
questions.explanation: Magnesium, preeclampsia maintenance: 1–2 g/hr. 4–6 g/hr is the loading amount used as an hourly rate. 3–4 g/hr is above the usual rate. 0.25–0.5 g/hr is too low.

questions.stem: Typical vasopressin bolus for refractory post-induction hypotension?
questions.explanation: Vasopressin, bolus: 0.5–1 unit. 40 units is the old cardiac arrest dose. 5–10 units is excessive for hypotension. 0.1 unit is too small.

questions.stem: Typical rocuronium maintenance redose?
questions.explanation: Rocuronium, maintenance: 0.1–0.2 mg/kg. 0.6 mg/kg is the intubating dose. 0.01–0.02 mg/kg is the vecuronium redose. 0.3–0.4 mg/kg is above the usual redose.

questions.stem: Initial dantrolene dose for MH?
questions.explanation: Dantrolene, initial: 2.5 mg/kg. 10 mg/kg is the cumulative point to reconsider. 5 mg/kg is double the initial dose. 1 mg/kg is the maintenance dose.

questions.stem: Concentration of carboprost?
questions.explanation: Carboprost vial: 250 mcg/mL. 200 mcg/mL is methylergonovine's concentration. 100 mcg/mL is diluted phenylephrine. 500 mcg/mL is double the vial strength. Source: Carboprost labeling.

questions.stem: Adult ondansetron PONV dose?
questions.explanation: Ondansetron, adult: 4 mg. 0.625 mg is the low droperidol dose. 10 mg is the metoclopramide dose. 8 mg is double the PONV dose.

questions.stem: Typical droperidol dose for PONV?
questions.explanation: Droperidol, PONV: 0.625–1.25 mg. 4–8 mg is the dexamethasone dose. 0.1–0.2 mg is too low. 2.5–5 mg is older higher doses with more sedation.

questions.stem: Concentration of succinylcholine?
questions.explanation: Succinylcholine vial: 20 mg/mL. 10 mg/mL is rocuronium's concentration. 2 mg/mL is cisatracurium's concentration. 100 mg/mL is sugammadex's concentration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Standard diluted dexmedetomidine infusion concentration?
questions.explanation: Dexmedetomidine infusion: 4 mcg/mL. 10 mcg/mL is diluted epinephrine. 16 mcg/mL is a norepinephrine infusion. 100 mcg/mL is the concentrate. Source: Dexmedetomidine labeling.

questions.stem: Onset of an IV thiopental induction dose?
questions.explanation: Thiopental, onset: 30–40 sec. 45–90 sec is IV lidocaine's onset. 2–3 min is vecuronium's onset. 10–15 min is dexmedetomidine's onset. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Duration of a single IV fentanyl dose?
questions.explanation: Fentanyl, duration: 30–60 min. 2–3 hr is hydromorphone's duration. 2–4 hr is morphine's duration. 3–10 min is remifentanil's duration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Typical IV epinephrine bolus for perioperative anaphylaxis, titrated?
questions.explanation: Epinephrine, anaphylaxis IV: 10–100 mcg. 0.3–0.5 mg is the IM dose. 1–2 mcg is too small. 1 mg is the cardiac arrest dose.

questions.stem: Concentration of rocuronium?
questions.explanation: Rocuronium vial: 10 mg/mL. 2 mg/mL is cisatracurium's concentration. 1 mg/mL is reconstituted vecuronium. 20 mg/mL is succinylcholine's concentration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Sugammadex dose for moderate block (TOF count 2)?
questions.explanation: Sugammadex, moderate block: 2 mg/kg. 4 mg/kg is the deep block dose. 16 mg/kg is the immediate reversal dose. 1 mg/kg is half the moderate block dose.

questions.stem: Onset of IV hydralazine?
questions.explanation: Hydralazine, onset: 10–20 min. 2–5 min is labetalol's onset. <1 min is phenylephrine's onset. 1–2 hr is too slow. Source: Hydralazine labeling and standard references.

questions.stem: Pediatric IV ketorolac dose (max 30 mg)?
questions.explanation: Ketorolac, pediatric: 0.5 mg/kg. 1 mg/kg is double the dose. 15 mg/kg is the pediatric acetaminophen dose. 0.1 mg/kg is too low.

questions.stem: Typical lorazepam dose per administration for status epilepticus (max 4 mg)?
questions.explanation: Lorazepam, status epilepticus: 0.1 mg/kg. 0.3 mg/kg is over the per-dose limit. 0.02 mg/kg is too low for status epilepticus. 0.2–0.3 mg/kg is the intranasal midazolam dose.

questions.stem: Concentration of IV famotidine (undiluted vial)?
questions.explanation: Famotidine vial: 10 mg/mL. 20 mg/mL is its dose misread as a concentration. 2 mg/mL is ondansetron's concentration. 5 mg/mL is metoclopramide's concentration. Source: Famotidine labeling.

questions.stem: Heparin dose before vascular cross-clamping?
questions.explanation: Heparin, vascular clamp: 100 units/kg. 50 units/kg is half the usual dose. 200 units/kg is double the usual dose. 300–400 units/kg is the bypass dose.

questions.stem: Typical ephedrine IV bolus?
questions.explanation: Ephedrine, bolus: 5–10 mg. 50–100 mcg is the phenylephrine bolus. 25–50 mg is excessive for a first bolus. 1–2 mg is too small.

questions.stem: Common promethazine concentration?
questions.explanation: Promethazine vial: 25 mg/mL. 12.5 mg/mL is its dose misread as a concentration. 2 mg/mL is ondansetron's concentration. 5 mg/mL is metoclopramide's concentration. Source: Promethazine labeling.

questions.stem: Adult IV epinephrine dose in cardiac arrest?
questions.explanation: Epinephrine, cardiac arrest: 1 mg. 100 mcg is an anaphylaxis IV bolus. 0.3–0.5 mg is the IM anaphylaxis dose. 3 mg is the old high-dose regimen.

questions.stem: Diluted phenylephrine concentration on the reference sheet (10 mg in 250 mL total)?
questions.explanation: Phenylephrine diluted (reference sheet): 40 mcg/mL. 10 mcg/mL is diluted epinephrine. 100 mcg/mL is a common syringe dilution. 16 mcg/mL is a norepinephrine infusion. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Sugammadex dose for deep block (PTC 1–2 or more, TOF 0)?
questions.explanation: Sugammadex, deep block: 4 mg/kg. 8 mg/kg is between the deep and immediate doses. 16 mg/kg is the immediate reversal dose. 2 mg/kg is the moderate block dose.

questions.stem: Adult metronidazole prophylaxis dose?
questions.explanation: Metronidazole, adult: 500 mg. 1 g is double the prophylactic dose. 250 mg is half the dose. 900 mg is the clindamycin dose.

questions.stem: IV magnesium dose for severe bronchospasm?
questions.explanation: Magnesium, bronchospasm: 2 g. 10 g is excessive. 4–6 g is the preeclampsia load. 1 g is half the dose.

questions.stem: Concentration of an ephedrine vial before dilution?
questions.explanation: Ephedrine vial: 50 mg/mL. 1 mg/mL is epinephrine 1:1,000. 5 mg/mL is the diluted bolus concentration. 10 mg/mL is phenylephrine's vial. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Peak effect of vecuronium at an intubating dose?
questions.explanation: Vecuronium, peak: 3–5 min. 60 sec is succinylcholine's peak. 1–3 min is rocuronium's peak. 25–40 min is vecuronium's duration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Phentolamine dose for vasopressor extravasation?
questions.explanation: Phentolamine, extravasation: 5–10 mg. 0.5–1 mg is too little for infiltration. 20–40 mg is excessive. 1–2 mg is small IV doses used for hypertension.

questions.stem: Typical naloxone titration dose for postoperative respiratory depression?
questions.explanation: Naloxone, postop titration: 40 mcg. 0.4 mg is the overdose starting dose. 10 mcg is too small to restore breathing. 4 mg is the intranasal dose.

questions.stem: Epinephrine concentration in a 1:200,000 solution?
questions.explanation: Epinephrine 1:200,000: 5 mcg/mL. 2.5 mcg/mL is the 1:400,000 concentration. 10 mcg/mL is the 1:100,000 concentration. 20 mcg/mL is the 1:50,000 concentration.

questions.stem: Pediatric cefazolin prophylaxis dose?
questions.explanation: Cefazolin, pediatric: 30 mg/kg. 10 mg/kg is the pediatric clindamycin dose. 15 mg/kg is the vancomycin dose. 50 mg/kg is above the usual pediatric dose.

questions.stem: Concentration of standard thiopental (2.5%)?
questions.explanation: Thiopental 2.5%: 25 mg/mL. 2.5 mg/mL is a misread of 2.5%. 50 mg/mL is a ketamine concentration. 10 mg/mL is propofol's concentration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Typical thiopental induction dose?
questions.explanation: Thiopental, induction: 3–5 mg/kg. 6–8 mg/kg is above the usual induction range. 1–2 mg/kg is the ketamine IV induction dose. 1.5–2.5 mg/kg is the propofol induction dose.

questions.stem: Typical intrathecal morphine dose for cesarean delivery?
questions.explanation: Morphine, intrathecal cesarean: 100–150 mcg. 10–25 mcg is the intrathecal fentanyl dose. 300–500 mcg is above the usual range. 2–3 mg is the epidural dose. Some centers use 50–100 mcg.

questions.stem: Concentration of 0.5% bupivacaine?
questions.explanation: Bupivacaine 0.5%: 5 mg/mL. 7.5 mg/mL is 0.75% bupivacaine. 0.5 mg/mL is a misread of 0.5%. 2.5 mg/mL is 0.25% bupivacaine. Source: Standard percent conversion.

questions.stem: Typical epidural morphine dose after cesarean delivery?
questions.explanation: Morphine, epidural: 2–3 mg. 6–8 mg is above the usual epidural dose. 100–150 mcg is the intrathecal dose. 0.2–0.5 mg is the IV hydromorphone increment.

questions.stem: Enoxaparin treatment dose given every 12 hr?
questions.explanation: Enoxaparin, treatment: 1 mg/kg. 40 mg is the prophylactic dose. 0.5 mg/kg is half the dose. 1.5 mg/kg is the once-daily treatment dose, not every 12 hr.

questions.stem: Onset of IV fentanyl?
questions.explanation: Fentanyl, onset: 1–3 min. 5–14 min is morphine's onset. 30–60 min is fentanyl's duration. 10–15 min is hydromorphone's onset. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Onset of an IV propofol induction dose?
questions.explanation: Propofol, onset: 30–40 sec. 60–120 sec is rocuronium's onset at intubating doses. 1–3 min is fentanyl's onset. 3–5 min is midazolam's peak. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Maximum dose of plain chloroprocaine?
questions.explanation: Chloroprocaine plain, max: 11 mg/kg. 7 mg/kg is the lidocaine with epinephrine maximum. 4.5 mg/kg is the plain lidocaine maximum. 14 mg/kg is the maximum with epinephrine. Some references cite 12 mg/kg.

questions.stem: Typical IM succinylcholine dose when there is no IV?
questions.explanation: Succinylcholine, IM: 4 mg/kg. 1–1.5 mg/kg is the adult IV dose. 8 mg/kg is double the IM dose. 2 mg/kg is the infant IV dose.

questions.stem: Flumazenil increment for benzodiazepine reversal, repeated every minute?
questions.explanation: Flumazenil, increment: 0.2 mg. 0.4 mg is the naloxone overdose start. 0.05 mg is too small to titrate effectively. 1 mg is the usual cumulative dose.

questions.stem: Onset of IV epinephrine?
questions.explanation: Epinephrine, onset: 30–60 sec. 2–5 min is labetalol's onset. 10–20 min is hydralazine's onset. 5–10 min is epinephrine's duration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Concentration of 0.25% bupivacaine?
questions.explanation: Bupivacaine 0.25%: 2.5 mg/mL. 5 mg/mL is 0.5% bupivacaine. 7.5 mg/mL is 0.75% bupivacaine. 0.25 mg/mL is a misread of 0.25%. Source: Standard percent conversion.

questions.stem: Pediatric dexamethasone PONV dose?
questions.explanation: Dexamethasone, pediatric: 0.15 mg/kg. 0.1 mg/kg is the pediatric ondansetron dose. 0.5 mg/kg is a croup-range dose. 0.05 mg/kg is too low.

questions.stem: Duration of epidural ropivacaine?
questions.explanation: Ropivacaine, epidural duration: 120–180 min. 60–120 min is epidural lidocaine's duration. 6–8 hr is too long for one epidural dose. 30–45 min is too short for epidural ropivacaine. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Onset of IV acetaminophen?
questions.explanation: Acetaminophen IV, onset: 15 min. 2–3 hr is too slow for IV onset. 1 hr is IV acetaminophen's peak. 4–6 hr is its duration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Duration of IV labetalol?
questions.explanation: Labetalol, duration: 2–4 hr. 5–15 min is labetalol's peak. 10–30 min is esmolol's duration. 8–12 hr is too long. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: First peripheral IV adenosine dose?
questions.explanation: Adenosine, first peripheral: 6 mg. 12 mg is the second dose. 18 mg is above the usual second dose. 3 mg is the central-line dose.

questions.stem: Typical preoperative pregabalin dose?
questions.explanation: Pregabalin, preop: 75–150 mg. 300–600 mg is the gabapentin dose. 200–400 mg is the celecoxib dose. 25 mg is too low.

questions.stem: Typical methadone dose at induction for opioid-sparing analgesia?
questions.explanation: Methadone, induction: 0.1–0.2 mg/kg. 0.03 mg/kg is too low for lasting effect. 0.3–0.4 mg/kg is above the studied range. 0.5–1 mg/kg is excessive.

questions.stem: Onset of IV hydromorphone?
questions.explanation: Hydromorphone, onset: 10–15 min. 2–3 hr is hydromorphone's duration. 30–40 sec is an induction agent's onset. 1–3 min is fentanyl's onset. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Nicardipine starting infusion rate?
questions.explanation: Nicardipine, start: 5 mg/hr. 15 mg/hr is the maximum rate. 2.5 mg/hr is the titration step. 1–2 mg/hr is the clevidipine start.

questions.stem: Methylene blue dose for methemoglobinemia?
questions.explanation: Methylene blue: 1–2 mg/kg. 0.1–0.2 mg/kg is too low. 3–4 mg/kg is above the usual range. 5 mg/kg is toxic-range dosing.

questions.stem: Peak effect of IV hydromorphone?
questions.explanation: Hydromorphone, peak: 10–20 min. 2–3 hr is hydromorphone's duration. 45–60 min is later than hydromorphone peaks. 3–5 min is fentanyl's peak. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Vancomycin prophylaxis dose?
questions.explanation: Vancomycin, prophylaxis: 15 mg/kg. 30 mg/kg is the pediatric cefazolin dose. 10 mg/kg is the pediatric clindamycin dose. 5 mg/kg is the gentamicin dose.

questions.stem: Concentration of 3% chloroprocaine?
questions.explanation: Chloroprocaine 3%: 30 mg/mL. 20 mg/mL is 2% chloroprocaine. 10 mg/mL is 1% lidocaine. 3 mg/mL is a misread of 3%. Source: Standard percent conversion.

questions.stem: Typical IV metoclopramide dose before induction?
questions.explanation: Metoclopramide, IV: 10 mg. 20 mg is the famotidine dose. 25–50 mg is the diphenhydramine dose. 4 mg is the ondansetron dose.

questions.stem: Clevidipine maximum labeled infusion rate?
questions.explanation: Clevidipine, max: 32 mg/hr. 16 mg/hr is where most patients are controlled. 64 mg/hr is double the labeled maximum. 15 mg/hr is the nicardipine maximum.

questions.stem: Concentration of 8.4% sodium bicarbonate?
questions.explanation: Sodium bicarbonate 8.4%: 1 mEq/mL. 2 mEq/mL is double the 8.4% strength. 0.5 mEq/mL is the 4.2% pediatric strength. 8.4 mEq/mL is a misread of 8.4%. Source: Standard formulation.

questions.stem: Typical IV succinylcholine dose for laryngospasm?
questions.explanation: Succinylcholine, laryngospasm: 0.1–0.5 mg/kg. 1.5–2 mg/kg is full intubating or infant dosing. 4 mg/kg is the IM dose. 1.2 mg/kg is the rocuronium RSI dose. Doses up to 1 mg/kg can be used.

questions.stem: Maximum dose of bupivacaine with epinephrine?
questions.explanation: Bupivacaine with epi, max: 3 mg/kg. 2.5 mg/kg is the plain maximum. 4.5 mg/kg is the plain lidocaine maximum. 7 mg/kg is the lidocaine with epinephrine maximum.

questions.stem: Concentration of fentanyl?
questions.explanation: Fentanyl vial: 50 mcg/mL. 100 mcg/mL is dexmedetomidine concentrate. 10 mcg/mL is a PCA or infusion dilution. 5 mcg/mL is bupivacaine-epinephrine's epinephrine content. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Typical IV ketamine induction dose?
questions.explanation: Ketamine, IV induction: 1–2 mg/kg. 0.1–0.5 mg/kg is the analgesic bolus. 2.5–3.5 mg/kg is above the usual IV range. 4–6 mg/kg is the IM induction dose.

questions.stem: Duration of an IV lidocaine bolus at induction?
questions.explanation: Lidocaine IV, duration: 10–20 min. 2–3 min is too brief. 60–70 min is spinal lidocaine's duration. 1–2 hr is IV lidocaine's half-life. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Typical haloperidol dose for PONV?
questions.explanation: Haloperidol, PONV: 0.5–2 mg. 5–10 mg is an agitation dose. 4–8 mg is the dexamethasone dose. 2.5–5 mg is above the low-dose antiemetic range.

questions.stem: Duration of IV glycopyrrolate (vagal blockade)?
questions.explanation: Glycopyrrolate, duration: 2–3 hr. 8–12 hr is too long. 30–60 min is atropine's duration. 60–120 min is neostigmine's duration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Gentamicin prophylaxis dose?
questions.explanation: Gentamicin, prophylaxis: 5 mg/kg. 1.5 mg/kg is an older traditional dose. 10 mg/kg is double the dose. 15 mg/kg is the vancomycin dose.

questions.stem: Duration of IV neostigmine?
questions.explanation: Neostigmine, duration: 60–120 min. 5–10 min is edrophonium-like duration. 2–3 hr is glycopyrrolate's duration. 4–6 hr is too long. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Typical cisatracurium intubating dose?
questions.explanation: Cisatracurium, intubation: 0.15–0.2 mg/kg. 0.02–0.05 mg/kg is a maintenance-range amount. 0.6 mg/kg is the rocuronium dose. 0.5 mg/kg is the atracurium dose.

questions.stem: Scopolamine transdermal patch strength?
questions.explanation: Scopolamine, patch: 1.5 mg. 0.4 mg is an older IV scopolamine dose. 3 mg is two patches. 1 mg is the amount delivered over 72 hr, not the patch content.

questions.stem: Typical alfentanil bolus for a brief procedure?
questions.explanation: Alfentanil, bolus: 10–20 mcg/kg. 0.1–0.5 mcg/kg is the sufentanil dose. 50–75 mcg/kg is induction-level alfentanil. 1–3 mcg/kg is the fentanyl dose.

questions.stem: IV lidocaine dose to blunt laryngoscopy?
questions.explanation: Lidocaine IV, laryngoscopy: 1–1.5 mg/kg. 4.5 mg/kg is the infiltration maximum. 3 mg/kg is the ropivacaine maximum. 0.5 mg/kg is a lower antiarrhythmic follow-up dose.

questions.stem: Peak effect of rocuronium at an intubating dose?
questions.explanation: Rocuronium, peak: 1–3 min. 3–5 min is vecuronium and cisatracurium peak. 30 sec is faster than any nondepolarizer peaks. 30–85 min is rocuronium's duration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Hydromorphone concentration on the reference sheet?
questions.explanation: Hydromorphone vial (reference sheet): 1 mg/mL. 10 mg/mL is morphine's concentration. 0.2 mg/mL is a PCA dilution. 4 mg/mL is a morphine strength. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Concentration of 0.75% (spinal) bupivacaine?
questions.explanation: Bupivacaine 0.75%: 7.5 mg/mL. 0.75 mg/mL is a misread of 0.75%. 5 mg/mL is 0.5% bupivacaine. 2.5 mg/mL is 0.25% bupivacaine. Source: Standard percent conversion.

questions.stem: Typical adult physostigmine dose for central anticholinergic syndrome?
questions.explanation: Physostigmine, adult: 0.5–2 mg. 4–5 mg is above the usual dose. 0.1–0.2 mg is too low to reverse the syndrome. 0.2 mg is the flumazenil increment.

questions.stem: Concentration of clevidipine?
questions.explanation: Clevidipine emulsion: 0.5 mg/mL. 0.1 mg/mL is premixed nicardipine. 10 mg/mL is propofol's concentration. 5 mg/mL is labetalol's concentration. Source: Clevidipine labeling.

questions.stem: Concentration of epinephrine 1:10,000 (the code syringe)?
questions.explanation: Epinephrine 1:10,000: 0.1 mg/mL. 0.4 mg/mL is atropine's concentration. 1 mg/mL is epinephrine 1:1,000. 10 mcg/mL is the diluted bolus syringe. Source: Standard ratio conversion.

questions.stem: Typical atracurium intubating dose?
questions.explanation: Atracurium, intubation: 0.5 mg/kg. 0.15–0.2 mg/kg is the cisatracurium dose. 1 mg/kg is double the usual dose. 0.1 mg/kg is the vecuronium dose.

questions.stem: Cefazolin prophylaxis dose for an adult under 120 kg?
questions.explanation: Cefazolin, adult under 120 kg: 2 g. 3 g is the dose for 120 kg or more. 1 g is an older, now underdosed amount. 500 mg is the metronidazole dose. Use 3 g for patients 120 kg or more.

questions.stem: Upper limit for a ketamine infusion for acute pain outside intensive monitoring (ASRA/AAPM/ASA 2018)?
questions.explanation: Ketamine, infusion ceiling: 1 mg/kg/hr. 0.35 mg/kg/hr is the bolus ceiling used as a rate. 0.5 mg/kg/hr is the top of the usual range. 2 mg/kg/hr is double the ceiling. Source: Schwenk et al. 2018.

questions.stem: Typical adult IV diphenhydramine dose?
questions.explanation: Diphenhydramine, IV: 25–50 mg. 100 mg is excessive. 6.25–12.5 mg is the promethazine dose. 5–10 mg is too low.

questions.stem: Maximum dose of ropivacaine?
questions.explanation: Ropivacaine, max: 3 mg/kg. 5 mg/kg is above the ropivacaine maximum. 4.5 mg/kg is the plain lidocaine maximum. 2.5 mg/kg is the plain bupivacaine maximum.

questions.stem: IV glucagon bolus for beta blocker overdose?
questions.explanation: Glucagon, beta blocker overdose: 3–10 mg. 20–30 mg is excessive. 1 mg is the hypoglycemia dose. 0.5 mg is too low.

questions.stem: Usual vecuronium concentration after reconstituting 10 mg in 10 mL?
questions.explanation: Vecuronium reconstituted: 1 mg/mL. 0.2 mg/mL is glycopyrrolate's concentration. 2 mg/mL is cisatracurium's concentration. 10 mg/mL is rocuronium's concentration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Peak effect of IV morphine?
questions.explanation: Morphine, peak: ~20 min. 3–5 min is fentanyl's peak. 45–60 min is later than morphine peaks. 2–4 hr is morphine's duration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Maximum subanesthetic ketamine bolus for acute pain (ASRA/AAPM/ASA 2018)?
questions.explanation: Ketamine, analgesic bolus: 0.35 mg/kg. 0.5 mg/kg is above the guideline bolus ceiling. 0.75 mg/kg is high enough to cause dissociation. 1–2 mg/kg is the induction dose. Source: Schwenk et al., Reg Anesth Pain Med 2018.

questions.stem: 20% lipid emulsion bolus for LAST in a patient over 70 kg?
questions.explanation: Lipid 20%, bolus over 70 kg: 100 mL. 250 mL is the follow-on infusion volume. 50 mL is half the bolus. 500 mL is above the bolus.

questions.stem: 20% lipid emulsion bolus for LAST in a patient under 70 kg?
questions.explanation: Lipid 20%, bolus under 70 kg: 1.5 mL/kg. 0.25 mL/kg is the per-minute infusion amount. 1 mL/kg is below the bolus dose. 3 mL/kg is double the bolus.

questions.stem: Typical intranasal midazolam dose for a child?
questions.explanation: Midazolam, pediatric intranasal: 0.2–0.3 mg/kg. 0.6–0.8 mg/kg is above the intranasal range. 0.5 mg/kg is the oral dose. 0.05 mg/kg is an IV sedation-range amount.

questions.stem: Usual cumulative flumazenil dose for the initial reversal series?
questions.explanation: Flumazenil, usual cumulative: 1 mg. 3 mg is the hourly maximum. 5 mg is above any recommended total. 0.2 mg is the single increment.

questions.stem: Heparin dose before cardiopulmonary bypass?
questions.explanation: Heparin, bypass: 300–400 units/kg. 5,000 units is the SC prophylaxis dose. 100 units/kg is the vascular dose. 600–800 units/kg is excessive.

questions.stem: Typical vecuronium intubating dose?
questions.explanation: Vecuronium, intubation: 0.1 mg/kg. 0.6 mg/kg is the rocuronium intubating dose. 0.01–0.02 mg/kg is the maintenance redose. 0.3 mg/kg is above the usual intubating dose.

questions.stem: Peak effect of IV acetaminophen?
questions.explanation: Acetaminophen IV, peak: 1 hr. 3 hr is too late. 15 min is IV acetaminophen's onset. 4–6 hr is its duration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Typical phenylephrine infusion rate?
questions.explanation: Phenylephrine, infusion: 10–100 mcg/min. 0.5–1 unit is the vasopressin bolus. 200–400 mcg/min is excessive. 1–2 mcg/min is too low.

questions.stem: Concentration of IV metoprolol?
questions.explanation: Metoprolol vial: 1 mg/mL. 5 mg/mL is labetalol's concentration. 10 mg/mL is esmolol's concentration. 20 mg/mL is hydralazine's concentration. Source: Metoprolol labeling.

questions.stem: Duration of succinylcholine at an intubating dose?
questions.explanation: Succinylcholine, duration: 4–6 min. 30–45 min is an intermediate nondepolarizer's duration. 60–90 min is longer than any normal succinylcholine block. 1 min is succinylcholine's half-life. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Duration of an IV phenylephrine bolus?
questions.explanation: Phenylephrine, duration: 5–10 min. 2–4 hr is labetalol's duration. <1 min is phenylephrine's onset. 30–60 min is atropine's duration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Adult IM epinephrine dose for anaphylaxis?
questions.explanation: Epinephrine, anaphylaxis IM: 0.3–0.5 mg. 10–100 mcg is the titrated IV bolus. 1 mg is the IV arrest dose. 0.1 mg is a small pediatric-size IM dose.

questions.stem: Onset of dexmedetomidine after a loading dose?
questions.explanation: Dexmedetomidine, onset: 10–15 min. 1–3 min is fentanyl's onset. 30–60 min is too slow. 30–60 sec is an induction agent's onset. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Regular insulin dose for hyperkalemia without ESRD?
questions.explanation: Insulin, hyperkalemia: 10 units. 2 units is too low. 5 units is the ESRD dose. 20 units is double the dose.

questions.stem: Typical oral sodium citrate volume before cesarean?
questions.explanation: Sodium citrate, oral: 30 mL. 100 mL is a fluid-bolus-size volume. 15 mL is half the usual volume. 60 mL is double the usual volume.

questions.stem: Duration of IV atropine?
questions.explanation: Atropine, duration: 30–60 min. 5–10 min is epinephrine's duration. 2–3 hr is glycopyrrolate's duration. 4–6 hr is too long for IV atropine. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Cumulative dantrolene dose after which other diagnoses are reconsidered?
questions.explanation: Dantrolene, cumulative: 10 mg/kg. 2.5 mg/kg is the initial dose. 5 mg/kg is half the cumulative point. 20 mg/kg is double the cumulative point.

questions.stem: Adult ACLS atropine dose for symptomatic bradycardia?
questions.explanation: Atropine, adult bradycardia: 1 mg. 0.1 mg is a small amount that can cause paradoxical slowing. 3 mg is the cumulative maximum. 0.5 mg is the older ACLS starting dose.

questions.stem: Typical esmolol loading dose?
questions.explanation: Esmolol, load: 0.5 mg/kg. 5 mg/kg is excessive. 50–300 mcg/kg/min is the infusion range. 0.1 mg/kg is too small.

questions.stem: Neostigmine dose for a shallow block (second twitch present) per the FDA label?
questions.explanation: Neostigmine, shallow block: 0.03 mg/kg. 0.5 mg/kg is an edrophonium-range dose. 0.01 mg/kg is too low for reliable reversal. 0.07 mg/kg is the dose for deeper block or longer-acting relaxants. Source: Bloxiverz FDA label.

questions.stem: Peak effect of an IV propofol induction dose?
questions.explanation: Propofol, peak: 60 sec. 3–5 min is midazolam's peak. 5 min is too late for propofol. 10–15 min is dexmedetomidine's onset. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Typical IV calcium gluconate dose?
questions.explanation: Calcium gluconate: 30 mg/kg. 100 mg/kg is excessive. 5 mg/kg is too low. 10 mg/kg is the calcium chloride dose.

questions.stem: Terbutaline SC dose for uterine tachysystole?
questions.explanation: Terbutaline, SC: 0.25 mg. 2.5–5 mg is the albuterol nebulizer range. 0.2 mg is the methylergonovine dose. 1 mg is above the usual dose.

questions.stem: Usual maximum neostigmine dose for reversal?
questions.explanation: Neostigmine, maximum: 5 mg. 2.5 mg is half the usual maximum. 7 mg is above the maximum. 10 mg is double the maximum.

questions.stem: Diluted ephedrine concentration (50 mg in 10 mL total)?
questions.explanation: Ephedrine diluted: 5 mg/mL. 50 mg/mL is the undiluted vial. 40 mcg/mL is diluted phenylephrine. 10 mg/mL is esmolol's concentration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Amiodarone dose for stable VT, given over 10 min?
questions.explanation: Amiodarone, stable VT: 150 mg. 300 mg is the pulseless arrest dose. 75 mg is half the stable dose. 450 mg is above the stable dose.

questions.stem: Typical sufentanil induction dose for noncardiac surgery?
questions.explanation: Sufentanil, induction: 0.1–0.5 mcg/kg. 1–3 mcg/kg is the fentanyl dose. 5–10 mcg/kg is cardiac high-dose range. 10–20 mcg/kg is the alfentanil bolus.

questions.stem: Concentration of 20% mannitol?
questions.explanation: Mannitol 20%: 200 mg/mL. 250 mg/mL is 25% mannitol. 100 mg/mL is 10% mannitol. 20 mg/mL is a misread of 20%. Source: Standard percent conversion.

questions.stem: Glycopyrrolate dose paired with each 1 mg of neostigmine?
questions.explanation: Glycopyrrolate per 1 mg neostigmine: 0.2 mg. 1 mg is the atropine bradycardia dose. 0.1 mg is half the pairing ratio. 0.4 mg is double the pairing ratio.

questions.stem: Duration of IV morphine?
questions.explanation: Morphine, duration: 2–4 hr. 8–12 hr is closer to methadone. 3–10 min is remifentanil's duration. 30–60 min is fentanyl's duration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Concentration of premixed nitroglycerin 50 mg in 250 mL?
questions.explanation: Nitroglycerin premix: 200 mcg/mL. 100 mcg/mL is the 25 mg/250 mL bag. 16 mcg/mL is a norepinephrine infusion. 400 mcg/mL is the 100 mg/250 mL bag. Source: Nitroglycerin premix labeling.

questions.stem: Concentration of IV amiodarone?
questions.explanation: Amiodarone vial: 50 mg/mL. 3 mg/mL is adenosine's concentration. 1.8 mg/mL is the premixed bag. 10 mg/mL is esmolol's concentration. Source: Amiodarone labeling.

questions.stem: Hydrocortisone stress dose for minor surgery?
questions.explanation: Hydrocortisone, minor surgery: 25 mg. 5 mg is too low. 50 mg is a moderate-surgery dose. 100 mg is the major-surgery dose.

questions.stem: Maximum dose of lidocaine with epinephrine?
questions.explanation: Lidocaine with epi, max: 7 mg/kg. 4.5 mg/kg is the plain maximum. 9 mg/kg is the topical airway limit. 11 mg/kg is the chloroprocaine maximum.

questions.stem: Concentration of IV acetaminophen?
questions.explanation: Acetaminophen IV: 10 mg/mL. 30 mg/mL is ketorolac's concentration. 1 mg/mL is a misread of 1,000 mg in 100 mL. 100 mg/mL is TXA's concentration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Concentration of 2% lidocaine?
questions.explanation: Lidocaine 2%: 20 mg/mL. 40 mg/mL is 4% topical lidocaine. 10 mg/mL is 1% lidocaine. 2 mg/mL is 0.2% ropivacaine. Source: Standard percent conversion.

questions.stem: Typical hyperbaric bupivacaine spinal dose for cesarean delivery?
questions.explanation: Bupivacaine, spinal cesarean: 10–15 mg. 2.5–3 mg is too little alone. 5–7.5 mg is a short urologic or ambulatory spinal amount. 20–25 mg is above the usual cesarean dose.

questions.stem: 4F-PCC dose range for warfarin reversal, by INR?
questions.explanation: 4F-PCC, warfarin reversal: 25–50 units/kg. 100 units/kg is the vascular heparin dose. 5–10 units/kg is too low. 60–80 units/kg is above the labeled range.

questions.stem: Typical adult IV ketorolac dose?
questions.explanation: Ketorolac, adult IV: 15–30 mg. 7.5–10 mg is too low. 60 mg is an older IM loading dose. 120 mg is the daily maximum.

questions.stem: Clinical duration of rocuronium 0.6 mg/kg (label median, range 15–85)?
questions.explanation: Rocuronium, duration: ~30 min. 4–6 min is succinylcholine's duration. 60–90 min is closer to pancuronium. ~10 min is too brief. Source: Rocuronium labeling.

questions.stem: Concentration of glycopyrrolate?
questions.explanation: Glycopyrrolate vial: 0.2 mg/mL. 0.4 mg/mL is atropine's concentration. 2 mg/mL is cisatracurium's concentration. 1 mg/mL is neostigmine's concentration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Typical IV midazolam premedication dose for a healthy adult?
questions.explanation: Midazolam, adult IV premed: 1–2 mg. 3–5 mg is excessive for premedication. 0.5 mg is an older-adult starting dose. 5–10 mg is an induction-range amount.

questions.stem: Concentration of a vasopressin vial?
questions.explanation: Vasopressin vial: 20 units/mL. 40 units/mL is double the vial strength. 0.2 units/mL is the diluted concentration. 10 units/mL is oxytocin's concentration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Typical cisatracurium infusion rate?
questions.explanation: Cisatracurium, infusion: 1–2 mcg/kg/min. 0.125–0.25 mcg/kg/min is too low to maintain block. 3–4 mcg/kg/min is above the usual range. 5–10 mcg/kg/min is an atracurium-range infusion.

questions.stem: Typical intrathecal fentanyl dose?
questions.explanation: Fentanyl, intrathecal: 10–25 mcg. 100–150 mcg is the intrathecal morphine dose. 2–5 mcg is too small. 50–100 mcg is an epidural bolus-range dose.

questions.stem: Dexamethasone concentration on the reference sheet?
questions.explanation: Dexamethasone vial (reference sheet): 4 mg/mL. 10 mg/mL is famotidine's concentration. 2 mg/mL is ondansetron's concentration. 5 mg/mL is metoclopramide's concentration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Subcutaneous heparin prophylaxis dose?
questions.explanation: Heparin, SC prophylaxis: 5,000 units. 40 mg is the enoxaparin prophylaxis dose. 10,000 units is double the dose. 1,000 units is too low.

questions.stem: Typical IV succinylcholine dose for an infant?
questions.explanation: Succinylcholine, infant IV: 2 mg/kg. 0.5 mg/kg is a laryngospasm-range amount. 4 mg/kg is the IM dose. 1 mg/kg is the dose for older children and adults.

questions.stem: Cefazolin prophylaxis dose for an adult 120 kg or more?
questions.explanation: Cefazolin, adult 120 kg or more: 3 g. 4 g is above the recommended dose. 1 g is an older underdosed amount. 2 g is the standard adult dose.

questions.stem: Maximum cumulative carboprost dose?
questions.explanation: Carboprost, cumulative max: 2 mg. 4 mg is double the maximum. 250 mcg is a single dose. 1 mg is half the maximum.

questions.stem: Onset of an IV ketamine induction dose?
questions.explanation: Ketamine, IV onset: 30–60 sec. 10–15 min is dexmedetomidine's onset. 3–5 min is closer to IM onset. 5–10 min is ketamine's duration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Propofol induction dose for a healthy adult under 55 (FDA label)?
questions.explanation: Propofol, adult induction: 2–2.5 mg/kg. 1–1.5 mg/kg is the dose for older, debilitated, or ASA 3–4 patients. 0.2–0.3 mg/kg is the etomidate induction dose. 2.5–3.5 mg/kg is the pediatric induction dose. Source: Diprivan FDA label. Many textbooks and the UK label give 1.5–2.5 mg/kg.

questions.stem: Upper limit of the IV succinylcholine dose used for laryngospasm?
questions.explanation: Succinylcholine, laryngospasm upper limit: 1 mg/kg. 4 mg/kg is the IM dose. 2 mg/kg is the infant intubating dose. 0.5 mg/kg is the top of the typical range. The typical dose is 0.1–0.5 mg/kg.

questions.stem: Typical etomidate induction dose?
questions.explanation: Etomidate, induction: 0.2–0.3 mg/kg. 1–2 mg/kg is the ketamine IV induction dose. 0.05–0.1 mg/kg is a sedation-level amount, too low for induction. 0.5–0.7 mg/kg is above the usual etomidate range.

questions.stem: Peak effect of IV midazolam?
questions.explanation: Midazolam, peak: 3–5 min. 10–20 min is hydromorphone's peak. 60 sec is propofol's peak. 15–80 min is midazolam's duration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Sugammadex dose for immediate reversal after an RSI dose of rocuronium?
questions.explanation: Sugammadex, immediate reversal: 16 mg/kg. 8 mg/kg is half the immediate dose. 32 mg/kg is double the immediate dose. 4 mg/kg is the deep block dose.

questions.stem: Typical vasopressin infusion rate in septic shock?
questions.explanation: Vasopressin, infusion: 0.03–0.04 units/min. 0.1–0.2 units/min is above the septic shock range. 0.5–1 units/min is the bolus amount used as a rate. 0.005–0.01 units/min is too low.

questions.stem: Usual starting remifentanil infusion rate for maintenance (FDA label)?
questions.explanation: Remifentanil, maintenance start: 0.25 mcg/kg/min. 0.04 mcg/kg/min is the starting rate in spontaneously breathing patients. 2.5 mcg/kg/min is above the labeled maximum. 0.5–1 mcg/kg/min is the induction rate. Source: Ultiva FDA label.

questions.stem: Typical IV fentanyl increment in PACU for an opioid-naive adult?
questions.explanation: Fentanyl, PACU increment: 25–50 mcg. 0.2–0.5 mg is the hydromorphone increment. 100–150 mcg is a large bolus for an opioid-naive patient. 5–10 mcg is too small to help.

questions.stem: Typical rocuronium intubating dose?
questions.explanation: Rocuronium, intubation: 0.6 mg/kg. 1.2 mg/kg is the RSI dose. 0.15–0.2 mg/kg is the cisatracurium dose. 0.1 mg/kg is the vecuronium intubating dose.

questions.stem: Commonly cited maximum topical lidocaine for awake airway topicalization (lean body weight)?
questions.explanation: Lidocaine, topical airway max: 9 mg/kg. 7 mg/kg is the maximum with epinephrine. 15 mg/kg is above the topical limit. 4.5 mg/kg is the plain infiltration maximum.

questions.stem: Concentration of ondansetron?
questions.explanation: Ondansetron vial: 2 mg/mL. 4 mg/mL is dexamethasone's concentration. 10 mg/mL is famotidine's concentration. 5 mg/mL is metoclopramide's concentration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Duration of an IV esmolol bolus?
questions.explanation: Esmolol, duration: 10–30 min. 4–6 hr is too long. 8–9 min is esmolol's half-life. 2–4 hr is labetalol's duration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Dextrose given with insulin for hyperkalemia?
questions.explanation: Dextrose with insulin: 25 g. 12.5 g is half the usual dextrose. 5 g is too little. 50 g is double the usual dextrose.

questions.stem: Initial remimazolam dose for procedural sedation, given over 1 min?
questions.explanation: Remimazolam, initial sedation: 5 mg. 10 mg is double the initial dose. 2.5 mg is the follow-up dose. 20 mg is far above the labeled start.

questions.stem: Concentration of the 30 mg ketorolac vial?
questions.explanation: Ketorolac 30 mg vial: 30 mg/mL. 50 mg/mL is diphenhydramine's concentration. 15 mg/mL is the 15 mg vial. 10 mg/mL is IV acetaminophen. Source: Ketorolac labeling.

questions.stem: Diluted vasopressin concentration on the reference sheet (20 units in 100 mL)?
questions.explanation: Vasopressin diluted: 0.2 units/mL. 20 units/mL is the undiluted vial. 0.04 units/mL is the infusion rate per minute misread as a concentration. 1 unit/mL is a common syringe dilution. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Typical IV labetalol increment for acute hypertension?
questions.explanation: Labetalol, increment: 5–20 mg. 1–2 mg is too small. 40–80 mg is later escalation doses, too large to start. 2.5 mg is the metoprolol starting increment.

questions.stem: Diluted epinephrine bolus concentration on the reference sheet?
questions.explanation: Epinephrine bolus syringe: 10 mcg/mL. 16 mcg/mL is a 4 mg/250 mL infusion. 100 mcg/mL is epinephrine 1:10,000. 5 mcg/mL is epinephrine 1:200,000. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Clevidipine starting infusion rate?
questions.explanation: Clevidipine, start: 1–2 mg/hr. 5 mg/hr is the nicardipine start. 16 mg/hr is a common upper titration point. 0.1–0.2 mg/hr is too low.

questions.stem: Duration after stopping a remifentanil infusion?
questions.explanation: Remifentanil, duration: 3–10 min. 2–3 hr is hydromorphone's duration. 30–60 min is fentanyl's duration. 60–90 min is far longer than remifentanil. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Procainamide loading infusion rate?
questions.explanation: Procainamide, rate: 20–50 mg/min. 1 mg/min is the amiodarone maintenance rate. 5 mg/min is too slow. 100–200 mg/min is too fast, risking hypotension.

questions.stem: Onset of IV lidocaine given during induction?
questions.explanation: Lidocaine IV, onset: 45–90 sec. 2–3 min is vecuronium's onset. 10–20 min is IV lidocaine's duration. 5–10 min is too slow for an IV bolus. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Mannitol dose for raised ICP?
questions.explanation: Mannitol, ICP: 0.5–1 g/kg. 0.1–0.2 g/kg is too low. 2–3 mL/kg is a hypertonic saline bolus volume. 1.5–2 g/kg is excessive.

questions.stem: Pediatric IV acetaminophen dose?
questions.explanation: Acetaminophen, pediatric IV: 15 mg/kg. 0.5 mg/kg is the pediatric ketorolac dose. 10 mg/kg is a lower oral dose. 40 mg/kg is a rectal loading dose.

questions.stem: Typical IV hydralazine dose?
questions.explanation: Hydralazine, IV: 5–10 mg. 1–2 mg is too small. 50 mg is an oral dose. 20–40 mg is an excessive first IV dose.

questions.stem: Recommended remifentanil concentration for adults after reconstitution and dilution?
questions.explanation: Remifentanil, adult dilution: 50 mcg/mL. 20–25 mcg/mL is the pediatric dilution. 10 mcg/mL is a fentanyl PCA dilution. 100 mcg/mL is dexmedetomidine concentrate. Source: Remifentanil labeling.

questions.stem: Onset of vecuronium at an intubating dose?
questions.explanation: Vecuronium, onset: 2–3 min. 8–10 min is too slow. 30–60 sec is succinylcholine's onset. 60–90 sec is close to rocuronium's onset. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Concentration of epinephrine 1:1,000?
questions.explanation: Epinephrine 1:1,000: 1 mg/mL. 10 mcg/mL is the diluted bolus syringe. 5 mcg/mL is epinephrine 1:200,000. 0.1 mg/mL is epinephrine 1:10,000. Source: Standard ratio conversion.

questions.stem: Maximum dose of plain bupivacaine?
questions.explanation: Bupivacaine plain, max: 2.5 mg/kg. 1.5 mg/kg is lower than the cited maximum. 4.5 mg/kg is the plain lidocaine maximum. 3 mg/kg is the maximum with epinephrine.

questions.stem: IV amisulpride dose for PONV rescue?
questions.explanation: Amisulpride, rescue: 10 mg. 5 mg is the prophylaxis dose. 20 mg is double the rescue dose. 4 mg is the ondansetron dose.

questions.stem: Duration of dexamethasone's effect?
questions.explanation: Dexamethasone, duration: 24–72 hr. 4–6 hr is IV acetaminophen's duration. 3.5–4.5 hr is dexamethasone's plasma half-life. ~12 hr is ondansetron's duration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Concentration of 10% calcium chloride?
questions.explanation: Calcium chloride 10%: 100 mg/mL. 1,000 mg/mL is a misplaced decimal. 27 mg/mL is its elemental calcium content. 10 mg/mL is a misread of 10%. Source: Standard percent conversion.

questions.stem: Hydrocortisone stress dose at induction for major surgery?
questions.explanation: Hydrocortisone, major surgery: 100 mg. 25 mg is the minor-surgery dose. 50 mg is the redose every 8 hr. 200 mg is the daily total in adrenal crisis.

questions.stem: Adult clindamycin prophylaxis dose?
questions.explanation: Clindamycin, adult: 900 mg. 1,200 mg is above the prophylactic dose. 500 mg is the metronidazole dose. 600 mg is a lower dose not used for adult prophylaxis.

questions.stem: Usual cumulative IV metoprolol dose for acute rate control?
questions.explanation: Metoprolol, cumulative: 15 mg. 30 mg is above the IV limit. 50 mg is an oral dose. 5 mg is a single increment.

questions.stem: Onset of rocuronium at an intubating dose?
questions.explanation: Rocuronium, onset: 60–120 sec. 30–60 sec is succinylcholine's onset. 3–5 min is vecuronium's peak. 5–7 min is slower than any intubating relaxant here. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: First IV diltiazem dose for AF?
questions.explanation: Diltiazem, first dose: 0.25 mg/kg. 0.35 mg/kg is the second dose. 1 mg/kg is excessive. 0.1 mg/kg is too low.

questions.stem: Onset of an IV phenylephrine bolus?
questions.explanation: Phenylephrine, onset: <1 min. 5–10 min is phenylephrine's duration. 2–5 min is labetalol's onset. 10–15 min is dexmedetomidine's onset. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Onset of an IV etomidate induction dose?
questions.explanation: Etomidate, onset: 30–60 sec. 2–3 min is cisatracurium's onset. 3–5 min is midazolam's peak. 10–15 min is dexmedetomidine's onset. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: IV magnesium dose for torsades?
questions.explanation: Magnesium, torsades: 1–2 g. 4–6 g is the preeclampsia load. 10 g is excessive. 200–500 mg is too low.

questions.stem: Nitroprusside infusion range?
questions.explanation: Nitroprusside, range: 0.3–10 mcg/kg/min. 15–20 mcg/kg/min is above the maximum. 0.01–0.1 mcg/kg/min is the epinephrine infusion range. 10–200 mcg/min is the nitroglycerin range. Limit the maximum rate to about 10 min.

questions.stem: Second peripheral IV adenosine dose?
questions.explanation: Adenosine, second: 12 mg. 18 mg is above the recommended second dose. 6 mg is the first dose. 24 mg is double the second dose.

questions.stem: Typical preoperative gabapentin dose?
questions.explanation: Gabapentin, preop: 300–600 mg. 75–150 mg is the pregabalin dose. 50–100 mg is too low. 1,200–1,800 mg is excessive preop.

questions.stem: Concentration of adenosine?
questions.explanation: Adenosine vial: 3 mg/mL. 1 mg/mL is metoprolol's concentration. 50 mg/mL is amiodarone's concentration. 6 mg/mL is the first dose misread as a concentration. Source: Adenosine labeling.

questions.stem: Typical IV hydromorphone increment for an opioid-naive adult?
questions.explanation: Hydromorphone, PACU increment: 0.2–0.5 mg. 2–4 mg is the morphine increment. 0.05–0.1 mg is too small to help. 1–2 mg is a large dose for an opioid-naive patient.

questions.stem: Duration of a single etomidate induction dose?
questions.explanation: Etomidate, duration: 4–8 min. 1–2 min is too brief. 30–60 min is fentanyl's duration. 15–80 min is midazolam's duration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Epinephrine content of a standard epidural test dose?
questions.explanation: Epinephrine, test dose: 15 mcg. 10 mcg is less than a standard adult test dose. 50 mcg is above a test dose. 5 mcg is the amount per mL at 1:200,000.

questions.stem: First adenosine dose through a central line?
questions.explanation: Adenosine, central line: 3 mg. 12 mg is the second peripheral dose. 1 mg is a heart transplant starting dose. 6 mg is the peripheral first dose.

questions.stem: Duration of IV midazolam?
questions.explanation: Midazolam, duration: 15–80 min. 4–8 min is propofol's duration. 2–4 hr is morphine's duration. 6–8 hr is closer to lorazepam. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Typical milrinone infusion range?
questions.explanation: Milrinone, infusion: 0.375–0.75 mcg/kg/min. 2–20 mcg/kg/min is the dobutamine range. 0.125–0.25 mcg/kg/min is too low. 1.5–3 mcg/kg/min is above the usual range.

questions.stem: Duration of spinal lidocaine?
questions.explanation: Lidocaine, spinal duration: 60–70 min. 2–3.5 hr is spinal ropivacaine's duration. 2–3 hr is spinal bupivacaine's duration. 10–20 min is IV lidocaine's duration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Morphine concentration on the reference sheet?
questions.explanation: Morphine vial (reference sheet): 10 mg/mL. 1 mg/mL is hydromorphone's concentration. 50 mcg/mL is fentanyl's concentration. 50 mg/mL is meperidine's concentration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Concentration of a phenylephrine vial before dilution?
questions.explanation: Phenylephrine vial: 10 mg/mL. 40 mcg/mL is the diluted bolus concentration. 50 mg/mL is ephedrine's vial. 1 mg/mL is epinephrine 1:1,000. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: TXA dose for postpartum hemorrhage, given over 10 min?
questions.explanation: TXA, PPH: 1 g. 10 mg/kg is an orthopedic weight-based dose. 2 g is double the dose. 100 mg is too low.

questions.stem: Common heparin concentration for IV boluses in the OR?
questions.explanation: Heparin, common vial: 1,000 units/mL. 10 mg/mL is protamine's concentration. 100 units/mL is a flush concentration. 5,000 units/mL is the SC prophylaxis vial. Source: Heparin labeling.

questions.stem: Glucagon dose for hypoglycemia without IV access?
questions.explanation: Glucagon, hypoglycemia: 1 mg. 0.1 mg is too low. 3–10 mg is the beta blocker overdose dose. 5 mg is excessive for hypoglycemia.

questions.stem: Typical edrophonium reversal dose?
questions.explanation: Edrophonium, reversal: 0.5–1 mg/kg. 0.04–0.07 mg/kg is the neostigmine dose. 0.1–0.2 mg/kg is too low for reversal. 2–3 mg/kg is above the usual dose.

questions.stem: Typical dexmedetomidine loading dose, given over 10 min?
questions.explanation: Dexmedetomidine, load: 1 mcg/kg. 3 mcg/kg is a high load that risks hypertension and bradycardia. 0.5 mcg/kg is half the usual load. 2 mcg/kg is double the usual load. Many clinicians skip the load.

questions.stem: Typical propofol infusion rate for MAC sedation?
questions.explanation: Propofol, MAC sedation: 25–75 mcg/kg/min. 100–200 mcg/kg/min is the TIVA maintenance range. 5–10 mcg/kg/min is too low to sedate. 0.2–0.7 mcg/kg/hr is the dexmedetomidine infusion range.

questions.stem: Typical IV famotidine dose for aspiration prophylaxis?
questions.explanation: Famotidine, IV: 20 mg. 4 mg is the ondansetron dose. 10 mg is the metoclopramide dose. 50 mg is the old IV ranitidine dose.

questions.stem: Onset of an IV ephedrine bolus?
questions.explanation: Ephedrine, onset: <1 min. 2–5 min is ephedrine's peak. 5–14 min is morphine's onset. 10–20 min is hydralazine's onset. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Magnesium loading dose for preeclampsia?
questions.explanation: Magnesium, preeclampsia load: 4–6 g. 0.5–1 g is too low. 1–2 g is the maintenance rate or torsades dose. 8–10 g is excessive.

questions.stem: Typical norepinephrine infusion rate?
questions.explanation: Norepinephrine, infusion: 0.01–0.5 mcg/kg/min. 2–20 mcg/kg/min is the dobutamine range. 0.03–0.04 units/min is the vasopressin infusion. 1–3 mcg/kg/min is excessive.

questions.stem: Time to TOF 0.9 after sugammadex 2 mg/kg at TOF count 2?
questions.explanation: Sugammadex, onset: ~2 min. 30–60 sec is succinylcholine's onset. 5–10 min is slower than sugammadex. 10–20 min is the time neostigmine typically needs. Source: Sugammadex labeling.

questions.stem: Concentration of cisatracurium (multidose vial)?
questions.explanation: Cisatracurium vial: 2 mg/mL. 20 mg/mL is succinylcholine's concentration. 10 mg/mL is rocuronium's concentration. 1 mg/mL is reconstituted vecuronium. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Concentration of enoxaparin prefilled syringes?
questions.explanation: Enoxaparin: 100 mg/mL. 10 mg/mL is protamine's concentration. 40 mg/mL is the prophylactic dose misread as a concentration. 1,000 units/mL is heparin's concentration. Source: Enoxaparin labeling.

questions.stem: Duration of IV acetaminophen?
questions.explanation: Acetaminophen IV, duration: 4–6 hr. 12 hr is ondansetron's duration. 1 hr is its peak. 2–4 hr is acetaminophen's half-life. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Protamine dose per 100 units of heparin?
questions.explanation: Protamine per 100 units heparin: 1 mg. 0.5 mg is a reduced ratio sometimes used late. 5 mg is excessive. 2 mg is double the ratio.

questions.stem: Onset of succinylcholine at an intubating dose?
questions.explanation: Succinylcholine, onset: 30–60 sec. 60–120 sec is rocuronium's onset. 2–3 min is vecuronium and cisatracurium onset. 4–6 min is succinylcholine's duration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Concentration of 0.2% ropivacaine?
questions.explanation: Ropivacaine 0.2%: 2 mg/mL. 2.5 mg/mL is 0.25% bupivacaine. 5 mg/mL is 0.5% ropivacaine. 0.2 mg/mL is a misread of 0.2%. Source: Standard percent conversion.

questions.stem: Midazolam vial concentrations?
questions.explanation: Midazolam vials: 1 or 5 mg/mL. 0.5 or 1 mg/mL is neostigmine's concentrations. 10 mg/mL is propofol's concentration. 2 mg/mL is etomidate's concentration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Duration of a thiopental induction dose?
questions.explanation: Thiopental, duration: 5–8 min. 30–60 min is fentanyl's duration. 1–2 min is too brief. 15–80 min is midazolam's duration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Typical IV nalbuphine dose for neuraxial opioid pruritus?
questions.explanation: Nalbuphine, pruritus: 2.5–5 mg. 0.5 mg is too small. 40 mcg is the naloxone titration dose. 10–20 mg is an analgesic dose with more mu reversal.

questions.stem: IV nitroglycerin bolus for uterine relaxation?
questions.explanation: Nitroglycerin, uterine relaxation: 50–100 mcg. 0.5–1 mg is excessive. 5–10 mcg is too small. 400 mcg is the sublingual tablet dose.

questions.stem: Clinical duration of cisatracurium 0.15 mg/kg?
questions.explanation: Cisatracurium, duration: ~55 min. 4–6 min is succinylcholine's duration. ~15 min is too brief. 90–120 min is closer to pancuronium. Source: Cisatracurium labeling.

questions.stem: Concentration of protamine?
questions.explanation: Protamine vial: 10 mg/mL. 100 mg/mL is TXA's concentration. 1 mg/mL is a misread of the dose ratio. 1,000 units/mL is heparin's concentration. Source: Protamine labeling.

questions.stem: Duration of IV hydromorphone?
questions.explanation: Hydromorphone, duration: 2–3 hr. 6–8 hr is too long. 30–60 min is fentanyl's duration. 3–10 min is remifentanil's duration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Onset of IV ondansetron?
questions.explanation: Ondansetron, onset: <30 min. 2 hr is ondansetron's peak. 4–8 hr is dexamethasone's antiemetic onset. 12 hr is ondansetron's duration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Concentration of 1% methylene blue?
questions.explanation: Methylene blue 1%: 10 mg/mL. 1 mg/mL is a misread of 1%. 5 mg/mL is 0.5% strength. 100 mg/mL is 10% strength. Source: Standard percent conversion.

questions.stem: Ketamine concentration on the reference sheet?
questions.explanation: Ketamine vial (reference sheet): 50 mg/mL. 25 mg/mL is thiopental's concentration. 20 mg/mL is succinylcholine's concentration. 5 mg/mL is midazolam's concentrated vial. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Typical rocuronium dose for rapid sequence induction?
questions.explanation: Rocuronium, RSI: 1.2 mg/kg. 0.6 mg/kg is the standard intubating dose. 0.9 mg/kg is between the standard and RSI doses. 2 mg/kg is above the usual RSI dose.

questions.stem: Adult dexamethasone PONV dose?
questions.explanation: Dexamethasone, adult PONV: 4–8 mg. 0.5–2 mg is the haloperidol PONV dose. 1–2 mg is too low. 10–20 mg is steroid dosing for airway edema.

questions.stem: Concentration of Dantrium after reconstitution (20 mg in 60 mL)?
questions.explanation: Dantrium reconstituted: ~0.33 mg/mL. 50 mg/mL is reconstituted Ryanodex. 3.3 mg/mL is a 6 mL dilution. 20 mg/mL is the vial content misread as a concentration. Source: Dantrium labeling.

questions.stem: Concentration of hydralazine?
questions.explanation: Hydralazine vial: 20 mg/mL. 1 mg/mL is metoprolol's concentration. 5 mg/mL is labetalol's concentration. 10 mg/mL is esmolol's concentration. Source: Hydralazine labeling.

questions.stem: Concentration of standard propofol (1%)?
questions.explanation: Propofol vial: 10 mg/mL. 25 mg/mL is thiopental's concentration. 2 mg/mL is etomidate's concentration. 20 mg/mL is the 2% formulation. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Concentration of 4% topical lidocaine?
questions.explanation: Lidocaine 4%: 40 mg/mL. 20 mg/mL is 2% lidocaine. 4 mg/mL is a misread of 4%. 50 mg/mL is 5% lidocaine. Source: Standard percent conversion.

questions.stem: Clinical duration of vecuronium 0.08–0.1 mg/kg?
questions.explanation: Vecuronium, duration: 25–40 min. 10–15 min is the redosing interval for maintenance doses. 4–6 min is succinylcholine's duration. 60–90 min is closer to pancuronium. Source: Vecuronium labeling.

questions.stem: Concentration of U-100 regular insulin?
questions.explanation: Regular insulin: 100 units/mL. 500 units/mL is U-500 insulin. 10 units/mL is a misread of U-100. 1 unit/mL is a common infusion dilution. Source: Insulin labeling.

questions.stem: Typical dobutamine infusion range?
questions.explanation: Dobutamine, infusion: 2–20 mcg/kg/min. 0.375–0.75 mcg/kg/min is the milrinone range. 0.01–0.5 mcg/kg/min is the norepinephrine range. 30–50 mcg/kg/min is above the usual range.

questions.stem: Concentration of dexmedetomidine concentrate (before dilution)?
questions.explanation: Dexmedetomidine concentrate: 100 mcg/mL. 10 mcg/mL is diluted epinephrine. 4 mcg/mL is the diluted infusion concentration. 50 mcg/mL is fentanyl's concentration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Concentration of diphenhydramine?
questions.explanation: Diphenhydramine vial: 50 mg/mL. 5 mg/mL is metoclopramide's concentration. 10 mg/mL is famotidine's concentration. 25 mg/mL is promethazine's concentration. Source: Diphenhydramine labeling.

questions.stem: Epinephrine concentration in a 1:400,000 solution?
questions.explanation: Epinephrine 1:400,000: 2.5 mcg/mL. 5 mcg/mL is 1:200,000. 10 mcg/mL is 1:100,000. 1.25 mcg/mL is 1:800,000. Source: Standard ratio conversion.

questions.stem: Duration of spinal bupivacaine?
questions.explanation: Bupivacaine, spinal duration: 2–3 hr. 6–8 hr is too long for a single spinal. 60–70 min is spinal lidocaine's duration. 4–6 hr is longer than a bupivacaine spinal lasts. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Onset of an IV vasopressin bolus?
questions.explanation: Vasopressin, onset: <1 min. 20 min is vasopressin's duration. 15 min is vasopressin's peak. 5–10 min is slower than its actual onset. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: IV meperidine dose range for postoperative shivering?
questions.explanation: Meperidine, shivering: 12.5–50 mg. 150 mg is above any shivering dose. 75–100 mg is an analgesic-range dose. 2.5–5 mg is the nalbuphine pruritus dose. The usual single dose is 25 mg.

questions.stem: Duration of IV ondansetron's antiemetic effect (reference sheet)?
questions.explanation: Ondansetron, duration: ~12 hr. 24–72 hr is dexamethasone's duration. 2 hr is ondansetron's peak. 3.5 hr is ondansetron's half-life. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Common atropine vial concentrations?
questions.explanation: Atropine vial: 0.4 or 1 mg/mL. 2 mg/mL is cisatracurium's concentration. 1 or 5 mg/mL is midazolam's concentrations. 0.2 mg/mL is glycopyrrolate's concentration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Onset of IV remifentanil?
questions.explanation: Remifentanil, onset: 1–2 min. 3–10 min is remifentanil's duration. 5–14 min is morphine's onset. 10–15 min is hydromorphone's onset. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Standard intranasal naloxone dose?
questions.explanation: Naloxone, intranasal: 4 mg. 0.4 mg is the IV overdose start. 0.2 mg is the flumazenil increment. 40 mcg is the postop IV titration dose.

questions.stem: Onset of IV esmolol?
questions.explanation: Esmolol, onset: 2 min. 10–30 min is esmolol's duration. 10 min is esmolol's peak. 20 min is too slow. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Duration of anesthesia after an IV ketamine induction dose?
questions.explanation: Ketamine, duration: 5–10 min. 1–2 min is too brief. 15–80 min is midazolam's duration. 30–60 min is fentanyl's duration. Source: Ketamine labeling and USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Adult hydroxocobalamin dose for cyanide toxicity?
questions.explanation: Hydroxocobalamin: 5 g. 2.5 g is half the dose. 10 g is the cumulative two-dose maximum. 1 mg is a B12 deficiency dose.

questions.stem: Albuterol delivered per MDI puff?
questions.explanation: Albuterol MDI, per puff: 90 mcg. 18 mcg is the ipratropium puff. 2.5 mg is the nebulizer dose. 200 mcg is more than one puff delivers.

questions.stem: Typical oral midazolam premedication dose for a child (max 20 mg)?
questions.explanation: Midazolam, pediatric oral: 0.5 mg/kg. 1 mg/kg is double the usual oral dose. 0.1 mg/kg is an IV-range amount, too low by mouth. 0.2–0.3 mg/kg is the intranasal dose.

questions.stem: Once-daily enoxaparin prophylaxis dose?
questions.explanation: Enoxaparin, prophylaxis: 40 mg. 5,000 units is the SC heparin dose. 1 mg/kg is the treatment dose. 80 mg is double the prophylactic dose.

questions.stem: Concentration of esmolol (ready-to-use vial)?
questions.explanation: Esmolol vial: 10 mg/mL. 5 mg/mL is labetalol's concentration. 250 mg/mL is the old concentrated ampule. 1 mg/mL is metoprolol's concentration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Typical IV promethazine dose for PONV?
questions.explanation: Promethazine, PONV: 6.25–12.5 mg. 1.25–2.5 mg is too low. 0.5–2 mg is the haloperidol dose. 25–50 mg is an older dose with more sedation and tissue risk.

questions.stem: Duration of a single propofol induction dose?
questions.explanation: Propofol, duration: 4–8 min. 15–80 min is midazolam's duration. 1–2 min is too brief. 30–60 min is fentanyl's duration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Concentration of metoclopramide?
questions.explanation: Metoclopramide vial: 5 mg/mL. 4 mg/mL is dexamethasone's concentration. 25 mg/mL is promethazine's concentration. 2 mg/mL is ondansetron's concentration. Source: Metoclopramide labeling.

questions.stem: Misoprostol dose for postpartum hemorrhage?
questions.explanation: Misoprostol, PPH: 600–1,000 mcg. 200 mcg is a single tablet. 2,000–3,000 mcg is excessive. 250 mcg is the carboprost dose.

questions.stem: Common meperidine concentration?
questions.explanation: Meperidine vial: 50 mg/mL. 50 mcg/mL is fentanyl's concentration. 10 mg/mL is morphine's concentration. 1 mg/mL is hydromorphone's concentration. Source: Meperidine labeling.

questions.stem: Concentration of flumazenil?
questions.explanation: Flumazenil vial: 0.1 mg/mL. 0.4 mg/mL is naloxone's concentration. 0.2 mg/mL is glycopyrrolate's concentration. 1 mg/mL is neostigmine's concentration. Source: Flumazenil labeling.

questions.stem: Typical initial IV naloxone dose for opioid overdose?
questions.explanation: Naloxone, IV overdose: 0.4 mg. 0.1 mg is a small titration step. 40 mcg is the postop titration dose. 4 mg is the intranasal dose.

questions.stem: Adult acetaminophen dose every 6 hr (50 kg or more)?
questions.explanation: Acetaminophen, adult: 1 g. 15 mg/kg is the dose for patients under 50 kg. 2 g is double the dose. 500 mg is half the dose.

questions.stem: Atropine dose paired with edrophonium?
questions.explanation: Atropine with edrophonium: 7–10 mcg/kg. 2–3 mcg/kg is too low to offset edrophonium. 20 mcg/kg is the pediatric bradycardia dose. 30–40 mcg/kg is enough to cause marked tachycardia.

questions.stem: Concentration of oxytocin?
questions.explanation: Oxytocin vial: 10 units/mL. 1 unit/mL is a diluted syringe. 20 units/mL is vasopressin's concentration. 30 units/mL is a 30-unit bag misread. Source: Oxytocin labeling.

questions.stem: Remifentanil infusion rate for induction with a hypnotic (FDA label)?
questions.explanation: Remifentanil, induction rate: 0.5–1 mcg/kg/min. 2–3 mcg/kg/min is above the labeled maximum. 0.25 mcg/kg/min is the maintenance starting rate. 0.04 mcg/kg/min is the spontaneous-breathing starting rate. Source: Ultiva FDA label.

questions.stem: Dantrolene maintenance dose after MH control, every 4–6 hr?
questions.explanation: Dantrolene, maintenance: 1 mg/kg. 2.5 mg/kg is the initial dose. 5 mg/kg is excessive. 0.1 mg/kg is too low.

questions.stem: Typical preoperative celecoxib dose?
questions.explanation: Celecoxib, preop: 200–400 mg. 800 mg is excessive. 75–150 mg is the pregabalin dose. 15–30 mg is the ketorolac dose.

questions.stem: Typical IV calcium chloride dose?
questions.explanation: Calcium chloride: 10 mg/kg. 3 mg/kg is too low. 50 mg/kg is excessive. 30 mg/kg is the calcium gluconate dose.
